resource.conclusion: Irregular, spiculated mass at 10 o'clock in the right breast, posterior depth, with associated architectural distortion. No suspicious calcifications. Left breast unremarkable. BI-RADS 5.

Right breast 10 o'clock, 6 cm from the nipple: irregular hypoechoic mass with angular margins, 1.9 x 1.5 cm. Right axilla: no morphologically abnormal lymph nodes. BI-RADS 5; ultrasound-guided biopsy recommended.
Right breast 10 o'clock, ultrasound-guided core biopsy: invasive ductal carcinoma, Nottingham grade 3. ER negative (0%), PR negative (0%), HER2 negative (IHC 0). Ki-67 approximately 70%.

Right breast partial mastectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy: invasive ductal carcinoma, Nottingham grade 3 (score 9/9), 2.3 cm. No lymphovascular invasion. Margins negative (closest 4 mm, posterior). Sentinel lymph nodes: 0 of 3 involved. pT2 pN0.
Germline multigene hereditary cancer panel (peripheral blood): no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified, including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, TP53, PTEN, CHEK2 and ATM.

Tumor genomic profiling (partial mastectomy specimen, with matched normal): TP53 c.743G>A (p.Arg248Gln), homozygous. No pathogenic alterations in PIK3CA, AKT1, PTEN, BRCA1 or BRCA2. Microsatellite stable. Detailed variant-level results are maintained on the genomics server, not in this report.
Post-lumpectomy and radiation changes in the right breast. No suspicious mass or calcifications. Left breast unremarkable. BI-RADS 2.

Multiple new bilateral pulmonary nodules, the largest 2.1 cm in the right upper lobe, highly suspicious for metastases. Enlarged subcarinal (1.6 cm) and right paratracheal (1.3 cm) lymph nodes. No pleural effusion. Post-surgical changes in the right breast.
